items.title: The majority of Tuvalu has applied to relocate to Australia to escape climate change. What happens now?
items.description: Tuvalu is building new land to hold back rising sea levels, but the majority of its people are applying to relocate to Australia. As they do, many are confronting a disturbing question.

items.title: Live: Paul Keating backs CGT changes as 'structurally sound'
items.description: Former prime minister Paul Keating says the government's changes to capital gains tax are "structurally sound" and seek to "arrest" the growth in house prices. Follow live.

items.title: Labor burns political capital as tax reform backlash grows
items.description: In an already difficult post-budget week, Labor isn't being helped by some of its "friends". But it has won an important endorsement from one powerful voice.

items.title: Pressure builds on new homes and inflation as costs go through the roof
items.description: Amid fast-rising prices — from materials craned in, to rubbish trucked out — a residential builder lists the costlier surcharges, levies and products hammering the construction industry and fuelling inflation.

items.title: El Niño looms as BOM releases long-range winter forecast
items.description: The Bureau of Meteorology is forecasting winter to be unusually warm across the entire country as an El Niño climate pattern is increasingly likely to take hold.

items.title: 'Survival mode all the time': Australian parents break taboos on raising kids
items.description: Almost 60 per cent of Australian parents are experiencing psychological distress, according to the largest-ever national survey of parents as the birth rate hits a record low

items.title: Trump's pick for ambassador to Australia names three priorities for role
items.description: David Brat, who rose to political prominence as part of the conservative Tea Party movement, takes questions from senators at a confirmation hearing.

items.title: Former Cuban president Raúl Castro indicted on murder charges in US
items.description: The move is the latest escalation in Washington's pressure campaign against the island's communist government.

items.title: Israeli minister taunts detained activists from Global Sumud Flotilla in video
items.description: Some of the detained activists were being pushed and dragged along the ground by Israeli forces while Itamar Ben-Gvir was taunting them.

items.title: WHO-linked report warns world more at risk of pandemic now than before COVID
items.description: As health leaders face deadly outbreaks of Ebola and hantavirus, a major report finds the world's response system remains dangerously underprepared.

items.title: Iran examining US proposal as Trump says talks in 'final stages'
items.description: Iran says it is examining the latest US proposal received from mediator Pakistan in talks to end the Middle East war, despite the two sides trading threats over resuming attacks.

items.title: They might look the same, but these penguins are very different
items.description: Gentoo penguins were thought to be a standalone species, but a new study says there are four distinct species — and it could lead to better conservation plans.

items.title: Photographer accused of stealing Bondi terror attack victim's camera
items.description: A photographer who allegedly stole a camera from a Bondi terror attack victim before pawning it days later has been charged.

items.title: Live: ASX is set to surge after Wall Street rallies
items.description: The Aussie share market is set to open strong after a rally on Wall Street. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: How to improve your home without stepping inside
items.description: Adding a new kitchen or bathroom to your home can be expensive, but budget constraints don't mean you have to take home improvement off the table altogether.

items.title: Can The Mandalorian and Grogu save Star Wars?
items.description: Grogu (aka Baby Yoda) made The Mandalorian a hit on streaming, now Disney is looking to parlay that goodwill into ticket sales to the latest Star Wars cinematic release.

items.title: Think you know music and film? Let's see how well you score in this quiz
items.description: From Mozart to Max Richter, can you pick the classical music in these iconic films?

items.title: Inside the 'worst managed infrastructure project in Australian history'
items.description: The Inland Rail has had funding slashed and the project placed on pause but Everald Compton has a bottle of Penfolds Grange waiting and even if it takes him till the age of 100, he's determined to see it through.

items.title: Snowtown killer James Vlassakis's image has been revealed. Here's why
items.description: The youngest of the Snowtown killers was the subject of a long-running suppression order that kept his face — or any description of his appearance — hidden for 25 years. Here's why that's been lifted.

items.title: WA gas users warn Labor not to repeat flaws in state reservation scheme
items.description: Western Australian gas users are urging the Albanese government to build stronger transparency and enforcement into its proposed national gas reserve scheme.

items.title: NT Health authorities MIA as diphtheria spreads across the outback
items.description: As diphtheria spreads across four different Australian jurisdictions in the largest outbreak since records began, public health messaging in the NT — the region most impacted by the serious disease — has been hard to come by.

items.title: Congo cancels World Cup farewell as US clarifies Ebola quarantine rules
items.description: The Congo football team cancels its farewell in Kinshasa as the US clarified what the rules would be for players and staff entering the country for the World Cup.

items.title: A year on, survivors still counting cost of '1-in-500-year' disaster
items.description: It was six months before Ed Trotter could return home after record floods on the NSW Mis North Coast. A year on from the disaster, others are still without working kitchens and bathrooms.

items.title: Aged care refunds for overcharging a 'burden' and 'total joke,' advocates say
items.description: Some advocates say the government's decision to delay price caps for at-home aged care services is a "burden".

items.title: Can Australia make its own fertiliser without fossil fuels?
items.description: Most fertiliser is a by-product of the oil industry, which is why it's so vulnerable to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. But there are other sources the industry could eventually switch to.
